name: Coin and button cells
summary: Small flat cells that keep clocks, remotes, scales and memory alive. Keep them from children: a swallowed cell burns the gut within hours.
uses: Clock and memory backup in computers and car keys
identify: Flat discs 5–25 mm across, marked CR2032, CR2025, LR44, SR626 and similar. Look on motherboards and in key fobs, kitchen scales, thermometers and glucose meters. CR cells are 3V lithium; LR and SR cells are 1.5V.
test: A fresh CR cell reads about 3V and an LR or SR about 1.5V. Below about 2.7V a CR cell is nearly flat. Test under a small load, like an LED, if you can.

decay.note: Sealed lithium coin cells lose only about 1% a year; cells left in devices drain faster.
